samples.summary: Blame tracker's extra repaint transaction reaches the unconditional local-selection publisher, adding a Yorkie presence write per edit
samples.evidence: `NoteBlameTracker.scheduleRepaint` (packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:210) dispatches one extra annotation-only transaction after every doc change whose labels changed. `NoteRemoteSelectionsPluginValue.update` (packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:110-119) has no `docChanged`/`selectionSet` guard: it calls `store.setLocalSelection(...)` on EVERY transaction, and `YorkieNoteStore.setLocalSelection` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:397-419) opens a `doc.update` each time. So enabling the gutter roughly doubles the per-keystroke presence/update traffic, and the extra transaction also lands right after an undo/redo restores the caret — the exact window the store documents as the "undo-vs-live-publisher race" (yorkie-note-store.ts:120-125). Neither the diff nor the design doc considers this consumer of the repaint transaction.

samples.summary: Backend/CLI whole-note replace wipes every per-run authorship attribute for the entire note
samples.evidence: `writeNoteRoot` does `text.edit(0, text.length, doc.content)` with no attributes (packages/backend/src/yorkie/note-content.ts:67). It is reached by the REST/CLI content PUT (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:187) and by "Make a copy" (packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:195). Any `notes.import` / content set, or a document copy, therefore resets the whole note's blame to `author: null` (blank gutter) — a silent, whole-document loss of the new metadata that the design doc's consequences list (docs/design/notes/notes.md:535-550) does not mention. Fix belongs on the backend write path (or on the doc).

samples.summary: Share-link notes route can never show the blame gutter and ignores the persisted preference
samples.evidence: `SharedNotesLayout` mounts `<NotesView readOnly={readOnly} viewMode={...} />` with no `showAuthors` prop and renders no `NotesToolbar` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:331-347), so the gutter is permanently off for share-link viewers/editors even though the same browser's persisted `wafflebase:notes:showAuthors` preference is on — while the very editors this feature attributes as "Anonymous" are the share-link ones. This is the only other `NotesView` consumer in the repo and the diff does not touch it.

samples.summary: Self-reported presence names still reach the DOM unsanitized outside the new boundary, so the "both render paths" claim is not exhaustive
samples.evidence: `display-name.ts:1-13` and docs/design/notes/notes.md:589-596 state that the two places a self-reported presence name reaches the DOM (gutter label, peer caret) both run through `sanitizeDisplayName`. The shared presence chrome renders `presenceData.presence.username` straight into the DOM at packages/frontend/src/components/user-presence.tsx:62/69/109 and :168 (and `alt=` attributes), from the same unverified Yorkie presence object that supplies `name`. Not a regression, but the newly-documented invariant ("no path puts an unverified name on screen unsanitized") does not hold repo-wide, and a reader of the new module will believe it does.

samples.summary: Per-keystroke label recompute is O(lines × runs) on the shared typing path once the gutter is on
samples.evidence: `NoteBlameTracker.update` calls `store.getAuthorSpans()` on every doc change; `YorkieNoteStore.getAuthorSpans` walks the whole `Text` run list (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:166-185) and `computeBlameLabels` runs `authorOfRange` — a linear scan over all spans — once per line (packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:96-118). Runs grow with edit count and are explicitly unbounded by design (docs/design/notes/notes.md:545-550), so on a long, heavily-edited note this becomes a lines×runs scan per keystroke inside the same update cycle as `noteSync`. Only when opted in, hence minor, but it lands on the editor's hot path rather than in isolated new code.

finding.summary: The new name-sanitization guard is bypassed by the peer caret label, which renders the same unverified presence `name` raw
finding.evidence: The delta adds `sanitizeAuthor()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:50) because the author name is a self-reported presence value that could smuggle control/zero-width/bidi characters or run unbounded. But the very same presence value reaches the DOM through a second, unguarded path: `YorkieNoteStore.getPeerSelections()` copies `peer.presence.name` verbatim (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:430) into `NotePeerSelection.name`, and `NoteCaretWidget.toDOM()` writes it straight into the caret label at packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:66 (`info.textContent = this.name;`) with no strip and no length cap. A hostile client that sets `presence.name` to `'a‮nd\nnb' + 'x'.repeat(500)` is neutralised in the blame gutter and untouched on its own caret label, which is rendered in the same editor. Either sanitize on the peer-name path too (in `getPeerSelections`, or centrally in `remote-selection.ts`), or scope the trust-boundary comment to say the caret label is deliberately left unsanitized.

verdict.reason: The alleged bypass does not exist. The only construction of `NoteCaretWidget` (packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:173-176) passes `sanitizeDisplayName(peer.name) ?? ''`, so the `info.textContent = this.name` write at remote-selection.ts:67 renders an already-sanitized value. `sanitizeDisplayName` (packages/notes/src/display-name.ts:31-56) performs exactly the strip (C0/C1 controls, Cf/bidi overrides, Cs, Co, Zl/Zp, plus extra invisibles), the Zs fold, and the 64-char cap the finding says are absent, so the hostile payload described is neutralised on the caret label too (asserted by packages/notes/src/display-name.test.ts:17 and :34). Grep for `NoteCaretWidget` across the repo finds no second live construction site — the only other hit is an archived design doc (docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260715-notes-markdown-type-todo.md:874). The finding's cited guard `sanitizeAuthor()` at yorkie-note-store.ts:50 also does not exist (line 50 is `MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`); the real guard is the shared `sanitizeDisplayName` imported at yorkie-note-store.ts:10, deliberately centralised at the DOM boundary, which is why `getPeerSelections()` at :434 legitimately copies the raw presence name. The comment scoping the finding requests is already present at yorkie-note-store.ts:38-39 and display-name.ts:1-13, which explicitly name the peer caret label as a shared consumer of the sanitizer.
